sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - Part 2 - June 15, 2026
summary: The sermon emphasizes that believers possess the same resurrection power of Christ within them and must understand their true identity as redeemed, righteous, and whole in Christ rather than broken or condemned.
Jesus teaches that life is not about accumulating possessions or fearing people's judgment, but about seeking God's kingdom first and trusting Him to provide all necessary things.

The pastor warns against hypocrisy, covetousness, and anxious thoughts about material needs, urging believers to recognize they are stewards of God's resources meant to bless others, not hoarders focused on self-preservation.

sermons.title: LIVE Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 5, 2026
summary: Jesus asks his disciples who they believe he is, and Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God, comes through divine revelation rather than human reasoning.
Jesus teaches that following him requires denying oneself, taking up one's cross, and being willing to lose one's life for his sake, which paradoxically leads to finding true life.
The sermon emphasizes that Satan can speak through even well-intentioned people, and believers must recognize and reject lies that contradict God's word and purpose.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 12, 2026
summary: Jesus heals a man born blind on the Sabbath, demonstrating that miracles transcend human tradition and religious law, and that faith requires both belief and obedient action.
The blind man's simple testimony—'I was blind, now I see'—proves more powerful than the Pharisees' theological arguments, showing that personal experience of God's power cannot be argued away.
The passage challenges believers to prioritize God's truth over human approval, to recognize that miracles still happen today, and to understand that faith without works is dead.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 1
summary: Saul's disobedience in offering a sacrifice he was forbidden to make cost him the kingdom, demonstrating that circumstances cannot justify violating God's commands.
The pastor emphasizes learning from biblical characters' mistakes rather than repeating them, using Saul's people-pleasing nature and fear of man as a cautionary example.
God's search for a man after His own heart—David—was initiated because of Saul's failure to obey, showing that disobedience has generational consequences.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 29
summary: God has already provided healing through Christ's stripes, and believers must take their God-given authority to command sickness to leave rather than begging God to heal them.
The power of spoken words aligned with God's authority is essential—believers must speak directly to their problems, not to God about their problems, following Jesus's teaching to speak to mountains.

Multiple testimonies demonstrate that when people stand in faith, speak with authority over their conditions, and refuse to accept the devil's lies, miraculous healings manifest immediately and permanently.

sermons.title: You Are Not Free to Do Whatever You Want | Andrew Wommack
summary: God has been faithful to America despite its flaws, and believers must recognize this goodness rather than focusing only on problems and negativity.
The root of societal decline is self-love and putting personal interests above God's kingdom, which manifests as failure to tithe, people-pleasing, and moral compromise.
True freedom and blessing come only through surrendering self-will to God's authority, speaking biblical truth boldly, and putting God's kingdom first in finances, decisions, and daily life.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 12, 2026
summary: Jesus teaches that walking in faith requires stepping out of the boat and trusting God even when circumstances appear dangerous, demonstrating that His power operates above natural limitations.
True ministry combines both the proclamation of God's word and the demonstration of supernatural power, as faith comes through hearing the word and witnessing God's works.
Believers must understand God's timing, exercise righteous judgment, and expect rejection when standing for truth, just as Jesus faced opposition despite His perfect representation of God.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - Part 1 - June 15, 2026
summary: The sermon emphasizes that true spiritual identity comes from understanding who you are in Christ through the Holy Spirit, not through external works or accomplishments, which revolutionizes how believers live and relate to God.
Jesus teaches that believers already possess healing, authority, and redemption through Christ's sacrifice, and the key is believing and acting on this truth rather than waiting for God to act.

The proper focus of Christian life is maintaining relationship with God above all else—whether through prayer, service, or daily decisions—because knowing God intimately matters more than any spiritual gift or material blessing.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 4
summary: Saul's disobedience to God resulted in his rejection as king and David's rise as his replacement, illustrating how God accomplishes His purposes even through human failure.
Samuel had to move past grieving Saul's rejection to fulfill God's new calling, teaching that believers should not let negative circumstances paralyze them from pursuing God's will.
God judges people by their hearts rather than outward appearance, choosing the weak and unqualified so that His power, not human ability, receives glory.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 26
summary: God has already provided healing through Christ's sacrifice, and believers must align their words and faith with this truth rather than begging God for what He has already done.
Allison's testimony demonstrates how releasing shame and speaking healing over oneself in faith produces physical restoration and transforms one's relationship with God.
The power of spoken words combined with genuine faith determines whether believers experience the blessings and protection God has promised in Scripture.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 25
summary: Colleen's testimony demonstrates how understanding God's unconditional love and grace became the foundation for her physical healing from chronic pain caused by failed back surgeries.
Andrew Wommack teaches that healing, like salvation, is an accomplished fact through Christ's atonement, not something believers must beg God to do in the future.
When believers shift from doubt about receiving healing to faith that they already possess it through Christ's stripes, they can stand firm against symptoms and receive their complete restoration.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - June 5, 2026
summary: Jesus prophesies his death and resurrection multiple times, teaching that true greatness in God's kingdom comes through humility and dependence on God rather than self-promotion.
Through the example of a child and warnings against offending the innocent, Jesus emphasizes that God values the humble and vulnerable, and that believers must adopt childlike dependence on God.

Jesus provides practical steps for reconciliation when conflicts arise, beginning with private conversation and progressing through witnesses and church involvement, demonstrating God's heart to restore broken relationships.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 27
summary: God's will is to heal everyone, and healing is available to all who believe and stand on God's word rather than their circumstances or symptoms.
Yvonne Smith's testimony demonstrates how faith, praise, and abiding in God's presence led to her healing from both breast cancer and multiple myeloma, even when symptoms temporarily returned.
When symptoms recur after healing, it is the enemy attempting to regain access through fear and doubt, not evidence that healing was lost or never occurred.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 3
summary: Saul's partial obedience to God's command to destroy the Amalekites demonstrates that partial obedience is actually disobedience, and his pride in taking credit for victory led to his rejection by God.
The sermon emphasizes that obedience to God is superior to sacrifice or good works, and that rebellion against God's word is as serious as witchcraft and idolatry.
Fear of man and people-pleasing cause believers to compromise God's truth, while humility and genuine obedience to God's voice are what bring His grace and blessing.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - July 20, 2026
summary: Jesus teaches that true discipleship requires complete commitment to God above all else, illustrated through parables about humility, counting the cost, and the parable of the lost sheep.
The sermon contrasts genuine conversion with superficial Christianity, emphasizing that being born again requires a heart change and desire to follow God, not merely external religious practices.

God's nature is revealed as gracious and seeking the lost, rejoicing over repentant sinners, while warning against self-righteousness and the hypocrisy of the Pharisees who rejected those Jesus welcomed.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 2
summary: God chose David as king eight years before his birth, demonstrating that He looks at the heart rather than outward appearance or qualifications, unlike how He initially chose the tall and impressive Saul.

Saul's repeated disobedience—first by offering sacrifice as a priest and later by refusing to completely destroy the Amalekites—shows that God does not force His plan upon people but allows free choice, even when it results in loss of blessing.

Every person has a God-given purpose written before their birth, regardless of their circumstances or perceived inadequacies, and this purpose is discovered through seeking God's will rather than self-determination.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 30
summary: Jolene's testimony demonstrates that healing comes through believing God's truth rather than relying solely on external prayer or ministry, as she was healed of cervical cancer by renewing her mind with the message of God's unconditional love and grace.

The pastor emphasizes that the same healing power available through personal ministry is accessible to anyone who gets hold of God's word and refuses to quit, regardless of their location or circumstances.

Believers must move from operating in fear and self-condemnation to understanding that Jesus has already done everything needed for healing, requiring only trust and persistent faith in God's promises.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 28
summary: God's will is to heal all people, as demonstrated through numerous testimonies of miraculous healings including cancer, autism, and various chronic illnesses.
Believers must move beyond conditional faith ('if it be your will') to confident belief that Jesus purchased healing through His stripes, and this healing is available to everyone.

The testimony of Xavier, a child healed of vaccine-related complications and sensory processing disorder, illustrates how faith in God's promises and prayer can restore families to wholeness and normal life.

sermons.title: 250 Years of Christian Liberty: Episode 1
summary: The Founding Fathers built America on biblical principles, with the Bible being the most cited source (34%) in their writings, far exceeding any other influence.
Early American colonies like Plymouth and Jamestown were explicitly Christian ventures, with the Geneva Bible and Puritan theology shaping the nation's religious and constitutional foundations.

America's 250-year stability and prosperity as the world's oldest constitutional republic stems directly from its biblical moorings, which were nearly lost through revisionist historical narratives taught in modern academia.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 5
summary: God chose David as king not based on outward appearance or family status, but because He looks at the heart rather than external qualifications.
Even when rejected by family and society, God's favor and anointing upon your life matters infinitely more than human opinion or validation.
Once God anoints and calls you, He supernaturally opens doors and accomplishes His purposes without requiring you to rely solely on natural means or human promotion.

sermons.title: Finding America Musical 2026 Livestream
summary: The musical traces America's spiritual foundation through figures like William Tyndale, the Pilgrims, and the Founding Fathers, showing how access to God's Word in common language empowered ordinary people to claim their identity as God's sons and daughters rather than subjects of kings.

From Tyndale's translation of Scripture to the Mayflower Compact to the Declaration of Independence, the narrative demonstrates that true liberty flows from knowing oneself through God's truth, not from political power or military might.

The performance calls modern Americans to remember that their nation was founded on the conviction that God's Word, freely available to all people, is the fixed point upon which all freedom and justice must stand.

sermons.title: Grace & Faith UK 2026 - S1
summary: The conference emphasizes that God's provision and healing are already complete; believers must open their hearts to receive what Christ has already accomplished through faith.
Testimonies like Chris Hall's miraculous recovery from paralysis demonstrate that standing on God's word produces breakthrough in physical, financial, and spiritual areas of life.

Participants are encouraged to sow financially into the kingdom with expectation, understanding that giving is not loss but a means of calling upon God to reveal abundance and prosperity in their lives.

sermons.title: Lessons from David: Episode 11
summary: David's humility after defeating Goliath contrasts sharply with Saul's pride and jealousy, demonstrating how pride opens the door to evil while humility attracts God's favor and blessing.

Jonathan and David form a covenant based on recognizing the same godly character traits in each other—particularly their willingness to honor God and others above themselves rather than promote their own interests.

Saul's insecurity and self-centeredness lead him to view David as a threat, initiating a 13-year period of persecution that marks the beginning of David's suffering despite his earlier triumph and public acclaim.

sermons.title: Healing Journeys: Episode 24
summary: God's will is for believers to be healed, and sickness is not a tool of God's correction but a result of living in a fallen world.
True healing comes not through striving and works of the law, but through resting in faith and trusting in the finished work of Jesus Christ.
Jeremiah Class's testimony demonstrates how surrendering the burden of trying to earn healing and focusing on relationship with God led to his miraculous deliverance from multiple sclerosis.

sermons.title: LIVE: Through the Bible with Andrew Wommack - July 29, 2026 - Part 1
summary: Jesus encounters a wealthy young ruler seeking eternal life and uses the man's attachment to money to reveal that his heart is divided—money has become his god rather than God himself.

Through comparison of Matthew, Mark, and Luke's accounts, the teaching clarifies that the problem is not wealth itself but trust in wealth; Jesus emphasizes that true discipleship requires surrendering everything to God.

The passage promises that those who sacrifice for God's kingdom receive a hundredfold return in this life plus eternal life, demonstrating God's generosity and the principle that giving, not hoarding, produces blessing.
